component.name: Software Next
component.summary: A faster GNOME Software, with full-screen screenshots (unofficial fork)

description.p: Software Next is an unofficial, experimental fork of GNOME Software that puts speed first. It finds, installs and updates the same software as GNOME Software (Flatpak apps, your distribution's packages through PackageKit, dnf5 or rpm-ostree, snaps and firmware), but its pages open almost at once.
Why use it instead of GNOME Software:

ul.li: Pages open much faster. In the fork's measurements the overview shows its apps in about 0.6 s instead of 3 s, a category's apps and icons appear in a fraction of a second instead of several seconds, and an app's details page is ready right away instead of after 2–3 s.
Search results appear as you type, in about 0.15 s.
Screenshots open full screen. Click a screenshot to see it over the whole window, zoom in on the details and move to the previous or next one.
It stays smooth. Long category lists scroll without stutter, and swiping back from a details page lands where you came from.
It is consistent. Every page shows the same state and progress of an app, and lists update in place instead of reloading.

description.p: It is not made or supported by the GNOME Software developers or the GNOME project, and its changes were developed with the help of generative AI. Please report problems to the fork.

It replaces the Software of your system: the desktop opens it for app details and search, and it checks for updates in the background once you turn that on. Your settings are shared with the system's Software.

Background updates replace the system's Software service with a user unit, ~/.config/systemd/user/gnome-software.service, which stays after the app is uninstalled and then starts the system's Software again. To go back, delete that file and run systemctl --user daemon-reload.

ul.li: screenshot-viewer: Move a swiped screenshot with the fingers
update-monitor: Run one daily update check at a time
flatpark: leave build-only files out of the tarball
details-page: Keep an installed app opened from a link on its source

description.p: Fixes Software never getting past the loading page on Fedora Atomic desktops (Silverblue, Kinoite and others): it now finds its rpm-ostree helper in the FlatPark build, and gives up with an error instead of waiting forever.
